en.title: Dune 3 and The Odyssey: A Secret Mythology Connects the Epics
en.summary: Two of 2026's most anticipated cinematic events, Denis Villeneuve's **Dune: Part Three** and the adaptation of Homer's **The Odyssey**, share a surprising, deep-rooted connection. The link lies not just in their epic scope, but in the very names of their central figures.
en.body:
As **Denis Villeneuve** gears up for **Dune: Part Three**, the cinematic world is abuzz with anticipation not only for his return to Arrakis but also for another colossal release slated for 2026: the adaptation of Homer's **The Odyssey**. While both films promise grand-scale adventures and compelling heroes, a closer look at the source material reveals a connection far more profound than shared cast members like **Zendaya** or a similar release year.

The key lies in the very name of **Dune**'s protagonist, **Paul Atreides**. The surname "Atreides" is not merely a label; it's a direct nod to the House of Atreus from Greek mythology. In Homer's epic poems, **The Iliad** and **The Odyssey**, "Atreides" is a patronymic title used repeatedly for two of the most prominent figures: **Agamemnon**, the king of Mycenae and leader of the Greek forces at Troy, and his brother, **Menelaus**, king of Sparta. This shared nomenclature suggests a deliberate thematic resonance between the ancient epic and Frank Herbert's seminal science fiction novel.

## Echoes of Ancient Tragedy

The mythological lineage of the House of Atreus is steeped in a cycle of betrayal, murder, and divine retribution, a narrative tapestry that seems to foreshadow the tragic destiny often associated with House Atreides in **Dune**. The family's history, originating with the cursed King Tantalus, is a grim saga of hubris and suffering. Tantalus's infamous test of the gods, involving the sacrifice and consumption of his own son Pelops, set in motion a chain of events that would plague his descendants for generations. This dark foundation of familial sin and divine punishment serves as a potent, albeit secret, prequel to the trials faced by **Paul Atreides** and his family, suggesting that the "founding curse" of the Atreides line might be an ancient, inescapable force.

## The Fan Connection

For fans of both **Dune** and classical literature, this revelation adds a fascinating layer of depth to Villeneuve's ambitious adaptation. The idea that **Dune: Part Three** could be viewed as a thematic sequel or companion piece to **The Odyssey** elevates the discussion beyond mere box office competition. It invites a deeper appreciation for the mythological underpinnings that have inspired science fiction for decades. The shared lineage, with **Agamemnon** being a distant ancestor to **Paul Atreides**, blurs the lines between ancient myth and futuristic saga, suggesting that the struggles for power, survival, and destiny are timeless themes that resonate across millennia and galaxies.

## What's Next

While **Dune: Part Three** is set for a December 18, 2026 release, details surrounding **The Odyssey**'s specific release date within 2026 are still emerging. Both films are poised to be major contenders, promising to captivate audiences with their epic narratives and directorial vision.

content_raw: With Christopher Nolan ‘s latest dominating the box office, cinema lovers aren’t just excited to learn what the director has planned next. They’re also excited about the second epic we have this year, another massive movie helmed by a filmmaker whose name evokes big ticket sales: Denis Villeneuve ‘s Dune: Part Three . It’s not hard to see the similarities, as both films feature mythic heroes on strange adventures, and they even share cast members in Zendaya and Robert Pattinson . However, fans of the books know that the connections between Dune and The Odyssey go deeper than one might expect. The secret is right there in the name of Frank Herbert ‘s lead character, Paul Atreides. The surname “Atreides” means “Son of Atreus,” referring to the Greek hero Atreus, father of Agamemnon and Menelaus. However, nothing is quite as it seems in either Greek mythology or the world of Dune , meaning the connections are far more complicated than just lineage. The Founding and Fall of the House of Atreus Fittingly enough for a story that leaves us longing for more, we have to begin with Tantalus, son of Zeus and Pluto. Tantalus established his family’s penchant for infanticide by killing his son Pelops, in order to test the gods. Most of the gods passed that test, except for the agricultural goddess Demeter, who actually ate some of the meal that Tantalus made out of Pelops. Infuriated, Demeter sentenced Tantalus to the underworld, where grapes and water remained forever out of reach, giving us the word “tantalizing.” His father punished, the gods resurrected Pelops, who later married Hippodamia by sabotaging her father’s chariot race, a decision that results in his line being cursed… which might account for the family killing that happens in the next generation. Pelops and Hippodamia give birth to Atreus and Thyestes, who kill their half-brother Chrysippus, and then get banished. Later, Atreus learns that his wife is having an affair with Thyestes, and also they’re fighting for the throne. So he channels his granddad and kills Thyestes’ sons and cooks them in a meal he serves to his brother, and then also engaged in incest, which eventually gets him killed. But not before he gives birth to two sons, Agamemnon and Menelaus. At this point, people who saw The Odyssey know about those guys, as Jon Bernthal stepped into the role of Menelaus, and Telemachus ( Tom Holland ) let Menelaus tell him something about Agamemnon (Benny Safdie), who sacrificed his daughter for good winds and got killed by his wife Clytemnestra ( Lupita Nyong’o ) because these Atreides boys never learn. So what does that have to do with Paul of Dune ? Paul’s Cyborg Great Granddad The first Dune novel takes place 20,000 years in the future, and while much has changed, humanity’s love of myths has not.
